title: Immediate Benefits to Singapore from Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership
what_it_is: Immediate Benefits to Singapore from Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership

sections.label: CPTPP economic benefits for Singapore
sections.summary: CPTPP offers Singapore business and market access gains, especially in Mexico and Canada, and is expected to raise exports and GDP by 0.2% by 2035.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The benefits include greater business and investment opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: It will also enhance market access opportunities for Singapore businesses in CPTPP markets, especially Mexico and Canada, with which Singapore does not currently have bilateral Free Trade Agreements (FTAs).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: For the 11 CPTPP countries as a whole, accounting for approximately 13.5% of the global economy and a market of 500 million people with a combined gross domestic product (GDP) of US$10 trillion, the Agreement is expected to generate an additional S$147 billion in global income.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: For Singapore, total exports and GDP are each expected to increase by 0.2% by 2035 arising from the CPTPP.

sections.label: Preferential tariffs for manufacturers
sections.summary: Processed food, textile and apparel manufacturers will benefit from preferential CPTPP tariffs, easier to qualify, in markets such as Japan, Australia and New Zealand.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Processed food, textile and apparel manufacturers, in particular, will benefit from preferential tariffs under CPTPP, which will be easier to qualify under CPTPP rules, to markets, such as Japan, Australia and New Zealand.

sections.label: Investor and procurement access gains
sections.summary: Investors gain from removal of foreign equity restrictions in certain CPTPP markets, and enterprises can bid for government procurement projects in Malaysia, Mexico and Vietnam.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Third, investors will benefit from the removal of foreign equity restrictions that would otherwise apply in certain CPTPP markets, such as the private healthcare, telecommunications, courier, energy and environmental services sectors in Brunei, Malaysia and Vietnam.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Fourth, enterprises will be able to bid for government procurement projects in Malaysia, Mexico and Vietnam, which were previously closed to foreign bidders.

sections.label: CPTPP ratification and entry into force
sections.summary: CPTPP enters into force after six countries ratify it, with three more expected this year and entry into force by the first quarter of next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: CPTPP will come into force shortly after six countries have ratified it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We are on track to see three more countries come on board by the end of this year and we should see this enter into force by the first quarter of next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: As for the US, our focus at this point in time is to get CPTPP to enter into force and, subsequently, the US can then make its decision as to whether it wishes to join.
